That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk tonight about what’s been happening? You don’t have to stay somewhere that’s harming you, but you also don’t have to figure everything out in one exhausted moment. ## 2

I understand why you might be skeptical, especially when institutions and media sometimes do make mistakes. But the evidence for a roughly spherical Earth doesn’t depend only on space photographs. Ships disappear over the horizon from the bottom up, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is round, and people have measured Earth’s curvature and circumnavigated it for centuries. Satellites, GPS, communications, and weather forecasting also rely on models that work because Earth is spherical. Photos from space are one line of evidence among many, not the foundation of the entire conclusion.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than red light does, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

That is why the sky usually looks blue during the day. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere before reaching us. Much of the blue light gets scattered away, leaving more red, orange, and pink light visible. The sky can look different on other planets because their atmospheres are made of different gases or contain different kinds of dust.
